p.t: In short
p.s: Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

p.t: Once the warehouse or supplier has processed an order, **changes are usually impossible**. Act before that point.

Take the customer's money only after you **confirm the item is in stock**.
After shipping, **never promise a cancellation**. Offer the return policy instead.

Refunds take **5 to 7 business days**. Tell customers this number.
If you **cannot reach a customer**, cancel the order and refund it.
Order states and what can still change
p.s: Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

p.t: **Not yet processed by fulfillment (the warehouse or supplier that packs and ships orders), not shipped**
Change possible?: Quantity, variant (a version of the product, such as a size or color), items and shipping details can usually still be changed, and cancellation is possible

What to do: **Make the change or cancel now**
**Processed by fulfillment, in transit (on the way) or shipped**
Change possible?: Changes are usually impossible
What to do: **Offer the replacement or return route** for the situation
Once an order has been processed by fulfillment, changes to quantity, variant, items or shipping details are usually impossible.
The requested change should still be made as soon as possible if it is still allowed.

Two terms first:
**Pre-authorisation**: a hold on the customer's card. The money is reserved but not taken yet.
**Capture**: actually taking the reserved money.
1. The customer places the order and gets a confirmation email.
p.h: Order flow from authorisation to tracking

p.t:
Their card gets a **pre-authorisation** (a hold, not a charge).
2. Supplier stock is checked automatically.
3. If the item is unavailable or on **backorder** (ordered now, but the supplier sends it later), **cancel the hold** (this is called voiding the pre-authorisation) and email the customer right away.
4. If the item is available, process the charges and submit the order for shipment within **5 business days** (working days, not weekends).
5. Email the tracking information within **24 hours** of shipment. Tracking is the code that shows where the parcel is.
6. If tracking has not arrived within **6 business days**, the customer may contact orders support.
Order confirmation emails send immediately upon checkout, indicating your order is in our system and your card is pre-authorized.
We immediately contact suppliers to verify stock availability. Backordered or unavailable items trigger authorization reversal and email notification to you.
Items available for shipment within 5 business days proceed through charge processing and dispatch to the warehouse.
Capture only after stock is confirmed
p.s: Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

p.t: Process orders as follows: pre-authorise the payment when the order comes in but do not charge yet.
Confirm the items are in stock with the supplier, then process the charge. If an item is out of stock, contact the customer with the expected wait time and charge only if they still want it.
This 2021 advice is older. It matches the 2025-era flow above, which also charges only after availability is confirmed.
If a customer orders while a supplier stock is unfinished, do not forward the order until stock is confirmed. Verify stock, then capture payment.
1. Call the number on the order and email the customer about the attempts.
p.h: Unconfirmable orders: Cancelling an order that cannot be confirmed

p.t: 2. If there is still **no response** before processing, cancel the order.

3. Send a cancellation email that lists the email and call dates and explains that the order was cancelled.
4. Consider adjusting product pricing in the meantime.

We did not hear back before we needed to process it, so unfortunately we have cancelled the order. If you still want the product, please reply or order again through our store.

offer a replacement purchase at 50% OFF using a discount link; invite further questions; sign off as the store customer support representative.

p.h: Cancellations before shipment: Cancelling an order that has not shipped

p.t: Open the order on the fulfillment platform (the system the warehouse or supplier uses) and check whether it has shipped.
2. If it has not shipped, **cancel it** on the fulfillment platform and refund the customer's payment.
3. Confirm to the customer that the order is cancelled and that the refund will be credited to their credit card within **5 to 7 business days**.
4. If it has already shipped, **do not promise a cancellation**. State the shipping date and that the order is in transit.
5. Explain that the store's refund and returns policy can be used once the order is delivered, and link the refund and returns policy page.

Shopify's "Cancel and refund" screen may show up to **10 days**. Shopify is the online store software. Tell the customer that timeframe, and expect refunds to usually arrive faster than the stated maximum.
Use the 5 to 7 business day figure in customer messages. Use the Shopify figure as the outer limit.

explain that cancellation is not possible after shipping; point to the return policy the customer can start once the order is delivered, with a link to the refunds and returns page; invite further questions;

**Do not promise to cancel** an order after it has shipped.
p.h: Do not promise cancellation after shipping

p.t: Offer the store's return or refund policy instead, which the customer can use after delivery. Cancellation promises for shipped orders lead to disputes and chargebacks.
A chargeback is when the customer's card company takes the money back from the seller.
Cancellation fee model (differs from the return-policy model)
p.s: Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

p.t: Cancellations initiated after 48 hours incur a $20 administrative fee regardless of
whether the order has shipped. If already shipped, the buyer covers return postage. Refunds are credited only to the original credit card used for the purchase.
Two models are documented:
**Fee model**: a **$20** administrative fee (a charge for paperwork and handling) for cancellations after 48 hours, shipped or not. For shipped orders, the buyer pays return postage.
**Return-policy model**: no cancellation once shipped. The customer starts a return after delivery under the store's refund and returns policy.
The sources do not say which model is preferred. Use the one that matches the store's written policy, and state it the same way in every reply.
When a customer cancels, **ask the real reason** instead of only refunding.

The answer can reveal product, price or experience barriers that affect conversion (the share of visitors who become buyers).
Handle cancelled orders as a learning opportunity:

1. **Contact the customer** and ask why they cancelled.
2. If they bought from a different retailer, ask what you could do better and use that to win the next sale.

3. If they bought from a brand you do not carry, contact that brand as a possible new supplier.
After a cancellation, work in this order:
1. Look for ways to improve the customer experience so the customer is more likely to return.
2. Find new suppliers so you can fill future orders for that product.
Without an automated cancellation system, handle cancellation and refund requests manually and respond quickly. Offer an updated ship date and alternatives before issuing a refund.
**Do not remove** out-of-stock products from the store.
p.h: Out-of-stock: listing and customer notice: Keep out-of-stock products visible

p.t: Either label them as out of stock with an expected availability date, or accept orders if you are willing to backorder and notify customers of the timeline.
Suppliers sometimes run out of stock of products that are still listed for sale.
p.h: Stock problem on an existing order

p.t: When a customer orders such a product, the order must go through the out-of-stock process rather than being shipped late without notice.
Early warning email (2023)
p.s: Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

p.t: Thanks for placing your order. Our warehouse confirmed that this product is on backorder.
The next delivery lands on [date], and we could dispatch the item to you on [date].
If you'd rather keep the order open, be aware that all online sellers source [brand]'s products from the same place, so the backorder applies at other shops too.
If you need the product sooner, we suggest [similar product], which is comparable because [reason], with a price gap of [amount].

You can: 1) wait for the item on [date], 2) switch to [similar product], or 3) cancel the order.
Send this email so the customer has **time to consider** before replying.
1. Ask the supplier **when the product will be available again**.
p.h: Out-of-stock: handling the order: Standard out-of-stock handling

p.t: Also ask whether a faster special order is possible and whether it costs extra.
2. **Contact the customer as soon as possible.** Tell them the product is not immediately available and how long the wait will be, then ask whether they are willing to wait.
3. If the customer is undecided about waiting, offer an authorised discount (a discount the business owner has approved) by refund if they wait.
4. If the customer cannot wait, look for a similar product that is in stock and suits their needs. If needed to close the sale, offer an authorised discount on the similar product.
5. If the customer will neither wait nor accept a similar product, **cancel the order** in Shopify. If payment was already captured, refund it.
6. If the customer is willing to wait, confirm with the supplier that you want to backorder the product, and ask the supplier to ship immediately once the product is back in stock.
7. If the supplier requires partial or full payment to place a backorder, **consult the business owner** and get authorisation before confirming any payment.
8. Once a backorder is placed, **email the customer** to confirm the order is on backorder and give the expected arrival date.
1. If a customer does not answer emails about an unavailable item, **try calling and texting**.
p.h: No response to an unavailable-item email

p.t: 2. If there is still no reply and the item is unavailable, **cancel and refund**.
Offering alternatives: two price values
p.s: Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

p.t: Procedure from 2025, when an item is out of stock with no clear delivery date:

1. Tell the customer about the stock problem.
2. Offer similar alternatives at about the same price. Example: **between 800 and 1,200 dollars** for a 1,000 dollar order.
3. If the customer wants a more expensive available item, send a Shopify draft order (an order you build in Shopify and send to the customer to pay) for the difference.
4. If the customer declines, cancel the order and refund it.

Rule for supplier failures: offer **2 or 3** alternative products that match the original in size, color, quality and price, and are in stock and ready to ship now. Ask whether they want to swap their order for one of them.
Use the 800 to 1,200 band in the 2025 procedure when the customer's order value is the reference.
Use the "match size, color, quality and price" standard when the customer must receive a like-for-like product.
Hi {customer name}, I am following up about your order {order number}.
We recently ran into a problem: our supplier is currently out of stock on this product and has no estimated restock date, [or: our supplier is not responding to us
and we are unable to fulfill this order for this specific product].

We would like to offer you two or three alternative products that are similar in size, color, quality and price and that are in stock and ready to ship right away: {alternative product 1}, {alternative product 2},
{alternative product 3}. Would you be willing to swap your order for one of these in-stock items? Please reply with your choice and we will ship it to you as soon as possible.
Orders placed **before** you learned of a supplier problem are the first ones to fix. Those customers are already waiting and can be offered a swap.
**Do not confirm any supplier payment** for a backorder without the business owner's authorisation.

p.t: **Discounts must be authorised** by the business owner.
Discounts, partial refunds and extra payment
p.s: Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

p.t: Only offer discounts that the business owner has authorised. A discount for waiting can be given as a refund.

A discount for a similar product can be used to close the sale.
To ask a customer for extra payment (for example, the price difference on an upgrade):

1. **Create a draft order** in Shopify with the amount you need.
2. **Send it** to the customer from Shopify so they can pay by the link.
Offer the **50% OFF** replacement purchase only through the discount link used in the template for in-transit orders.
When an order came from a short product test, **tell the customer directly**.
p.h: Product test orders and pre-order follow-up

p.t: Offer a pre-order option so they can keep the item. A pre-order means the customer reserves a product that is not in stock yet. The following email is the 2025-26 template for that case.
Subject: Thank you for your order - important update about [Product name] Hi [Customer name], Thank you very much for your order of [Product name] (order number [Order number]).

We really appreciate your trust in us. We need to tell you something important: this order was part of a short product test to find out whether the product sells before we buy it in larger quantities.
Your payment of [Order amount] will be refunded in full to your original payment method. You should see the refund within [Refund timeframe].
If you would still like to receive this product, please reply to this email and tell us. We will then place you on a pre-order list, and the expected delivery is around [Expected delivery window].

You will be the first to know if anything changes, and you can cancel at any time before shipping. Thank you for your patience and understanding. Best regards, [Your name] [Store name] [Support email]
**Gifts from Amazon:** do not ship free gift items directly from Amazon to the customer, because the Amazon origin is visible.
Have the items shipped to yourself, repackage them, and include a note for the customer.

When a product is out of stock but already ordered, a gift of a different slow-selling design keeps the customer happy until the stock arrives. Once the stock comes in, **resend the item** the customer originally bought.
